title: Label of a restricted junta example
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{\\pm1\\}$ be a Boolean function, let $P\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$ be a set of coordinates, and fix signs $z_i$ for $i\\in P$. Suppose a sample consists of an input $x\\in\\{-1,1\\}^n$ and a sign label, with $x_i=z_i$ for every $i\\in P$, and suppose its label equals $f(x)$. Then the label equals the value of the restriction of $f$ to the free coordinates, evaluated at the sample's free-coordinate assignment.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$P$ is a finite set of coordinates
$z$ assigns a sign to each coordinate in $P$
the sample input agrees with $z$ on $P$
the sample label equals the value of $f$ on the sample input
